claim: Structured reflection (compare findings against each candidate diagnosis) helps in specific conditions (availability bias in second-years; one-week retention) but can hurt at first, and the availability-bias induction failed in a larger replication. Gap search: the only independent availability-bias trial (46 residents, 2020) induced the bias but reflection did not repair it; other replications come from the originating group.
agent_test: Run the compare operator on bias-induced cases (similar prior case in context) at equal tokens; check the effect only when a primer is present.

claim: Correct diagnoses are reached faster than wrong ones within the same clinician; longer deliberation signals difficulty or error, not care. LLM side: length marks error in one 7-error sample (p=.032) but prompted extra reasoning raises o1 accuracy, so length is a symptom, not a cause.
schema_part: S0 (long run = warning sign, not safety)
agent_test: Log tokens per item; test whether length predicts error and whether a length-triggered escalation helps.

claim: The default-interventionist timeline (fast wrong answer, slow correction) is challenged: reasoners often give correct logical answers fast under load and detect conflict even when wrong; Feeling of Rightness predicts rethinking. Bago and De Neys exact percentages still unread (abstract only). LLM analogue: a second pass without an outside signal does not improve answers (GSM8K 75.9 to 74.7, CSQA 75.8 to 41.8).
schema_part: S0 mode choice via a confidence/conflict signal
agent_test: Compare mode switch on a confidence signal (sample agreement) vs a question-type rule at equal tokens.

claim: Intuition is reliable only in regular environments with long practice and feedback; confidence is not a guide to accuracy.
agent_test: Route items by environment regularity (checkable/known type) vs by self-reported confidence; compare error rates.

claim: In clinical text tasks CoT lowers accuracy for most models (82 of 95), with drops growing with reasoning length; best models fall least.
agent_test: Cap reasoning length on clinical items; compare capped vs uncapped at equal tokens.

claim: Named clinical reasoning styles (intuitive, analytic, differential, Bayesian) do not beat plain CoT for GPT-4 on MedQA (76% vs 72-78%, all p>.05) and hurt GPT-3.5 (analytic -6, differential -8, Bayesian -4).
agent_test: Replicate style prompts on our model at equal tokens.

claim: Planted cognitive-bias cues lower LLM medical accuracy in every model tested (GPT-4 72.7% base; GPT-4 mean -5.4 points, GPT-3.5 mean -18.6 points = -37.4% relative; false consensus worst). A short warning or demonstration restores most of GPT-4's loss (gap 5.4 to 1.8 or 0.8 points) and little for weaker models. Absolute points and relative percent are mixed in the paper's text.
agent_test: Run BiasMedQA with and without the scaffold's challenge step.

claim: Explicit fast/slow agents with rule-coded switches (stuck 5 steps, invalid action, critical decision) beat slow-only agents at fewer tokens on ScienceWorld (84.7 vs 45.3 best baseline; 757 vs 1,856-2,983 tokens/action). Gap search: a 2026 medical dual-system pipeline (chat model for history, o1-mini for the answer) gained up to +38.7 points under a planted patient anchor, but o1-mini alone (85.1% biased) beat every dual setup and no tokens were matched; AdaptThink learns a thinking switch on math (-53% length, +2.4% accuracy).
agent_test: Implement code-checked switch rules in our loop; compare to always-slow at equal tokens.

claim: Pre-filtering input to strip opinion and irrelevant text (System 2 Attention) restores accuracy lost to distractors (62.8 to 80.3; 51.7 to 61.3).
agent_test: Add a rewrite-then-answer step on distractor-laden items.

claim: Slow-method outputs can be distilled into direct answers on some tasks (last-letter 30.0 to 98.0) but fail on hard math (GSM8k 9.40% direct).
agent_test: Cache solved routines as direct shortcuts; test on repeated-type items.

claim: Reasoning models overthink easy items (1,953% more tokens on 2+3); self-training cut tokens 48.6% at equal accuracy.
agent_test: Add an easy-item shortcut; measure token saving at equal accuracy.

claim: The Cognitive Reflection Test traps fast answers in people: about 41% correct in the original, 38% in a replication, 44% of medical students all correct.
agent_test: Use CRT variants as an S0 sanity probe.

claim: Human time-pressure promotion of intuitive cooperation failed to replicate in a 21-lab registered replication (ITT -0.37 points vs original 8.6), so 'fast = intuitive = X' claims are fragile.
schema_part: S0 (do not rely on speed effects)
agent_test: None direct; treat speed manipulations as weak.

claim: Dual-process claims in medicine mix two readings: process (System 1 bias, System 2 fix) and knowledge (both run on stored cases); the evidence favours knowledge and says errors come from both types. Gap search: retrieval of documents (32 snippets) did not beat CoT on MedQA-US (GPT-4 83.97 to 82.80, Mixtral 64.10 to 60.02); similar-case retrieval at equal tokens is untested.
agent_test: Test knowledge injection (retrieved similar cases) vs extra deliberation at equal tokens.

claim: A planted wrong anchor (patient self-diagnosis) is better resisted by swapping in a reasoning model for the last step than by prompts or lower temperature, but the swap is confounded with model strength and was not token-matched.
agent_test: Run the same biased dialogues with (a) strong reasoning model alone, (b) cheap model plus challenge step, (c) cheap model plus reasoning only on conflict, matched on tokens.

claim: Stated model confidence is a poor mode-routing signal: most LLMs answer 5 out of 5 on nearly all medical items; where it varies it tracks accuracy (GPT-4o high-confidence 83.2% vs medium 45.9%).
agent_test: Compare routing by verbal confidence, by sample agreement, and by an external check, against always-reason and never-reason at equal tokens.

claim: No published study tests mode routing (fast vs slow chosen per item) against always-slow and never-slow at matched tokens on medical diagnosis; the nearest data are cost-accuracy Pareto curves (MedQA 88/92/96% at roughly $5/$50/$500).
agent_test: Build the router test: easy-first single pass, escalate on disagreement of 3 samples; count tokens.

claim: On open-ended cases a reasoning model lists the right diagnosis in its differential far more often than it ranks it first (NEJM CPC: 78.3% in list vs 52% first), so ranking, not recall, is the weak step.
agent_test: Add a rank-and-challenge step after the differential; compare top-1 accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: A forced challenge and differential step with named roles (devil's advocate, premature-closure facilitator) recovered 76% top-2 accuracy from 0% initial on 16 bias-linked case reports, but the start is zero by case selection and no equal-token single-agent control exists.
agent_test: Replicate with a single agent given the same extra tokens, on cases not selected for first-answer failure.

claim: Reflection and bias-fix effects in human diagnosis are mostly reported by one research group; the one independent availability-bias trial found the bias but no repair, and a large trial found no bias induction.
schema_part: O (reflection step: test, do not assume)
agent_test: Test reflection on LLM diagnosis separately for easy and hard items.

claim: Clinicians anchor on their own first differential even with AI help (AMIE alone top-10 59.1% vs unassisted 33.6%; assisted 51.7%), so the first draft differential should not be passed on without a challenge.
agent_test: Hide the first draft differential from the verify step in one arm and compare.
